cautions: Both candidates are amorphous glasses, not anisotropic crystalline minerals.
No material is selected as a preferred TMC1A fit.
Downloaded tabulation spans 0.2-500 micron, narrower than the historical 0.1-3000 micron temperature grid.
MCFOST 4.1.13 holds n,k constant below minimum wavelength and extends each with its endpoint log-log slope above maximum.
This numerical extension is not laboratory evidence and requires sensitivity checks before physical inference.
Bulk densities differ from historical Draine density; this changes opacity per dust mass as well as spectral shape.
A new temperature solution is required after changing material; old temperature fields are not reusable for a self-consistent model.
MCFOST Tsub in the header is not measurement temperature, and the current physical template disables sublimation.
The unchanged laboratory H2O companion has zero k values and only extends to 19.94054 micron; combined use needs explicit numerical and coverage checks.
citation: Dorschner, Begemann, Henning, Jaeger & Mutschke (1995), Astronomy & Astrophysics 300, 503

H2O_30K_Leiden_mcfost.dat.zero_k_policy: original zero values preserved; logarithmic interpolation risk, not silently floored
